concerns.text: FR-001 cites OpenML dataset ID 2352, whereas the idea explicitly references OpenML dataset ID 42123. This changes the primary data source and may alter available features and target variables, constituting a drift from the original research scope.

FR-004 specifies outlier removal using a Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rule, while the idea’s methodology sketch calls for ±3 σ outlier removal. The differing statistical rule modifies the preprocessing pipeline and drifts from the intended analysis.

FR-015 introduces nested cross‑validation (inner/outer loops). The idea only mentions a single 5‑fold cross‑validation for hyper‑parameter tuning; adding nested CV expands the methodological scope beyond what was proposed.

FR-010 adds a formal power analysis (α = 0.05, effect size d = 0.5, σ = 1) and a conditional switch to Wilcoxon testing based on power < 0.8. The idea’s statistical plan only conditions on sample size (< 200) for choosing Wilcoxon; the power analysis is an extra requirement not requested.

FR-016 requires verification of fallback roughness columns via a Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test. The idea does not mention any fallback data handling, so this adds a new validation step outside the original scope.

FR-018 forbids using aggregate material property features alongside their raw constituents to avoid multicollinearity. The idea never specifies the use of aggregate features, making this a new constraint not part of the original research question.

FR-017 mandates storing all final results in a canonical `results.json` file as the Single Source of Truth. The idea does not require a specific results storage format, so this introduces an engineering artifact beyond the scope of the research plan.
